data.one_liner: A Flutter compass plugin using device sensors to provide real-time heading and accuracy.
data.what_it_does: Provides real-time device heading in degrees (0-360) using built-in device sensors. It automatically compensates for device orientation changes, offers camera-mode heading for augmented reality, and exposes sensor accuracy and hardware availability.
use_when: You need to build a compass or directional UI in Flutter.
Your application requires augmented reality or camera-mode orientation headings.
You need orientation-compensated heading readings from device sensors.
avoid_when: The target devices lack physical compass or rotation sensors.
You only require standard geolocation coordinates without magnetic heading.
strengths: Orientation-aware and automatically compensates for device rotation changes.
Exposes camera-mode heading for AR or camera overlays.
Tunable update presets to balance smoothness and battery consumption.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific location permissions on iOS.
Depends on physical hardware sensors which are not available on all devices.
data.setup_notes: iOS requires location permission strings in Info.plist. Android usage of fine location is optional depending on features.

alternatives.name: sensors_plus
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides raw accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer sensor streams if you need to build custom sensor processing instead of a dedicated compass.
